english: let the punishment fit the crime

terms.comment: Literally “let the penalty be equal to the offence”.
Traupman’s variant of Cicero’s law, with culpae for noxiae. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
